    {
      "id": "core:12:word:1",
      "supportEnglish": "bill",
      "sourceSpanish": "cuenta",
      "targetFrench": "l'addition",
      "kind": "term",
      "noteEnglish": "Spanish source note: in Mexico and the US, people say la cuenta; in Spain also la nota in some places. In French, l'addition is the bill you ask for in a café or restaurant. It is not the receipt (le reçu)."
    },
    {
      "id": "core:12:word:2",
      "supportEnglish": "cover charge",
      "sourceSpanish": "cubierto",
      "targetFrench": "les frais de couvert",
      "kind": "term",
      "noteEnglish": "In this lesson's story, the café lists a cover charge on its menu. Treat it as part of this story, not as a general rule about cafés."
    },
    {
      "id": "core:12:word:3",
      "supportEnglish": "tip",
      "sourceSpanish": "propina",
      "targetFrench": "le pourboire",
      "kind": "term",
      "noteEnglish": "In this lesson's story, the waitress says the tip is optional. That describes this one café bill; tipping customs differ from place to place."
    },
    {
      "id": "core:12:word:4",
      "supportEnglish": "service charge",
      "sourceSpanish": "servicio",
      "targetFrench": "le service",
      "kind": "term",
      "noteEnglish": "This is the word used in the Reader: Le service n'est pas compris (service is not included). Les frais de service names a service fee listed as a separate line on a bill. In this story, the statement that service is not included applies to this café only."
    },

      "id": "core:12:word:13",
      "supportEnglish": "Could you bring me the bill, please?",

      "kind": "phrase",

      "supportEnglish": "What is this charge?",

      "kind": "phrase",

      "sourceSpanish": "Quiero pagar en efectivo.",
      "targetFrench": "Je voudrais payer en espèces.",
      "kind": "phrase",
      "noteEnglish": "The meaning is 'I want to pay in cash.' Je voudrais is the polite conditional of vouloir (literally 'I would like'); it softens the literal Quiero / Je veux, which can sound abrupt when said to a server. The literal present form, Je veux payer en espèces, is shown in the verb forms for vouloir."

  "reader": [
    {
      "id": "core:12:line:1",
      "supportEnglish": "After eating breakfast, the traveler raises his hand and says: Excuse me, could you bring me the bill, please?",
      "sourceSpanish": "Después de desayunar, el viajero levanta la mano y dice: Disculpe, ¿me trae la cuenta, por favor?",
      "targetFrench": "Après son petit-déjeuner, le voyageur lève la main et dit : « Excusez-moi, pourriez-vous m'apporter l'addition, s'il vous plaît ? »"
    },
    {
      "id": "core:12:line:2",
      "supportEnglish": "The waitress answers that he can pay at the register or at the table, as he prefers.",
      "sourceSpanish": "La mesera responde que puede pagar en la caja o en la mesa, como prefiera.",
      "targetFrench": "La serveuse répond qu'il peut payer à la caisse ou à la table, comme il préfère."
    },
    {
      "id": "core:12:line:3",
      "supportEnglish": "When the bill arrives, the traveler sees an extra charge and asks: What is this charge?",
      "sourceSpanish": "Cuando llega la cuenta, el viajero ve un cargo extra y pregunta: ¿Qué es este cargo?",
      "targetFrench": "Quand l'addition arrive, le voyageur voit un supplément et demande : « À quoi correspond ce supplément ? »"
    },
    {
      "id": "core:12:line:4",
      "supportEnglish": "The waitress explains that it is the cover charge, and that the menu states it on the last page.",
      "sourceSpanish": "La mesera explica que es el cubierto, y que el menú lo indica en la última página.",
      "targetFrench": "La serveuse explique qu'il s'agit de frais de couvert, indiqués à la dernière page de la carte."
    },
    {
      "id": "core:12:line:5",
      "supportEnglish": "The traveler says he understands, but he wants to know if the tip is included.",
      "sourceSpanish": "El viajero dice que entiende, pero quiere saber si la propina está incluida.",
      "targetFrench": "Le voyageur dit qu'il comprend, mais il veut savoir si le pourboire est compris."
    },
    {
      "id": "core:12:line:6",
      "supportEnglish": "She answers that service is not included, so the tip is optional.",
      "sourceSpanish": "Ella contesta que el servicio no está incluido, así que la propina es opcional.",
      "targetFrench": "Elle répond que le service n'est pas compris ; le pourboire est donc facultatif."
    },
    {
      "id": "core:12:line:7",
      "supportEnglish": "Since he has no cash, the traveler asks: Can I pay by card?",
      "sourceSpanish": "Como no tiene efectivo, el viajero pregunta: ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?",
      "targetFrench": "Comme il n'a pas d'espèces, le voyageur demande : « Puis-je payer par carte ? »"
    },
    {
      "id": "core:12:line:8",
      "supportEnglish": "The waitress brings the card terminal, he pays, and he asks her for the receipt.",
      "sourceSpanish": "La mesera trae la terminal, él paga y le pide el recibo.",
      "targetFrench": "La serveuse apporte le terminal de paiement ; il paie et lui demande le reçu."
    },
    {
      "id": "core:12:line:9",
      "supportEnglish": "Before leaving, the traveler checks the total and says thank you.",
      "sourceSpanish": "Antes de salir, el viajero revisa el total y da las gracias.",
      "targetFrench": "Avant de partir, le voyageur vérifie le total et dit merci."
    }
  ],

The spellings with y (je paye, ils payent) are also accepted. Paying by card is par carte; paying in cash is en espèces."

      "supportEnglish": "I ask for the receipt before leaving.",
      "explanationEnglish": "Demander is a regular -er verb. It means to ask for something (demander le reçu) or to ask (demander si...). The pattern is demander quelque chose à quelqu'un, as in the Reader: il lui demande le reçu (he asks her for the receipt). No word for 'for' is added. Despite the resemblance, demander is an ordinary 'ask', not as strong as English 'demand'."

      "politeVousForm": "apportez",
      "frenchExample": "Pourriez-vous m'apporter l'addition, s'il vous plaît ?",
      "supportEnglish": "Could you bring me the bill, please?",
      "explanationEnglish": "Apporter is a regular -er verb meaning to bring something to someone. In Pourriez-vous m'apporter l'addition ?, apporter is an infinitive after pourriez-vous (could you), and the pronoun m' (to me) goes directly before that infinitive. For a conjugated form, see the Reader: La serveuse apporte le terminal de paiement. Apporter is used for things you carry; for bringing a person, French uses amener."
    },
    {
      "sourceSpanishInfinitive": "incluir",
      "frenchInfinitive": "inclure",
      "meaningEnglish": "to include",
      "frenchForms": {

      "politeVousForm": "incluez",
      "frenchExample": "La carte indique que l'addition inclut les frais de couvert.",
      "supportEnglish": "The menu says the bill includes the cover charge.",
      "explanationEnglish": "Inclure is the direct equivalent of incluir. It is irregular: the singular forms end in -s, -s, -t (j'inclus, tu inclus, il inclut). For amounts on a bill or menu, French also very commonly uses comprendre, especially as être compris: Le service est compris ; Le pourboire est-il compris ? Both verbs are correct for 'include'. The example sentence belongs to this lesson's story."
    },
    {
      "sourceSpanishInfinitive": "querer",
      "frenchInfinitive": "vouloir",
      "meaningEnglish": "to want",
      "frenchForms": {
        "je": "veux",
        "tu": "veux",
        "il_elle_on": "veut",
        "nous": "voulons",
        "ils_elles": "veulent"
      },
      "politeVousForm": "voulez",
      "frenchExample": "Je veux payer en espèces.",
      "supportEnglish": "I want to pay in cash.",
      "explanationEnglish": "Vouloir is irregular: the stem is veu- in the singular (veux, veux, veut), voul- in nous voulons and vous voulez, and veul- in ils veulent. Je veux is the literal present-tense match for Quiero and is shown here to teach the form. When speaking to a server, the conditional Je voudrais payer en espèces is the more polite choice, which is why the phrase card uses it."
    }
